title: Selling fees (eBay US)
supports: Fetched (page shows no effective date). 250 zero insertion fee listings a month, then $0.35; final value fee for most categories 13.6% up to $7,500 plus 2.35% above, plus $0.30 per order ($10 or less) or $0.40; fee charged on the total including shipping and sales tax; Below Standard adds 6% (7% after four months); $20 dispute fee; 1.65% international fee.

title: Seller performance policy
supports: Fetched. Seller levels; evaluation on the 20th of each month; transaction defect rate up to 2%; cases closed without seller resolution up to 0.3% or 2; Top Rated thresholds; Below Standard consequences; eBay Live transactions excluded from 15 October 2026; appeals within 30 days.

title: eBay Money Back Guarantee policy
supports: Fetched. Item not received and not as described: buyers have 30 days; sellers respond within 3 business days; refunds within 2 business days of receiving a return; evidence for non-receipt (tracking, delivery scan, signature for $750 or more); appeal within 30 days of eBay's decision.

title: Feedback policy
supports: Fetched. Fake, misleading or manipulated feedback is not allowed; feedback must reflect the buyer's actual experience; removal requests within 90 days of the transaction; negative or neutral feedback does not affect seller performance.

title: ItemType (Trading API reference)
supports: Fetched (two parts). Up to 24 pictures at no cost in almost any category; no HTML or JavaScript in titles. The page gives no title length, so none is stated in the kit.

title: Referral fees
supports: Fetched. No setup or monthly fees; referral fee by category, some tiered by price; charged on the total sales price including shipping and handling; category rate table (for example Everything Else 15%, Consumer Electronics 8%, Apparel 5%, 10% or 15% by price).

title: Walmart Marketplace (home and FAQ)
supports: Fetched. Seller qualifications: business tax ID (not a Social Security Number), documents for business name and address, a selling track record, GTINs or UPCs from GS1 company prefixes, compliance with the Prohibited Products Policy, fulfilment through WFS or a US warehouse that handles returns, a compatible payment processor.

title: Listing Quality dashboard
supports: Fetched. Score at catalogue and item level covering content, discoverability, offer, ratings and reviews, plus post-purchase quality insights; improvement list (category and attributes, clear title, descriptions, high-resolution photos, shipping speed, competitive price, reviews).

title: Seller Performance Standards
supports: Fetched. Measured over 30 or 60 days: cancellation 2% or below, on-time delivery 90% or above, valid tracking 99% or above, response to customers within 48 hours 95% or above, negative feedback 2% or below, returns 6% or below (9% for resold), item not received 2% or below, late shipment 5% or below; failing to act may lead to suppression, suspension or termination.

title: Pricing Insights overview
supports: Fetched (last updated 19 June 2026). Price competitiveness compares the offer with comparable external prices including shipping; an offer is competitive at the same or a lower price; "Price not competitive" is a reason for Buy Box ineligibility; unpublished items are listed with reasons.

title: Repricer
supports: Fetched. Free strategy-based repricing tool; sellers set minimum and maximum prices per item; Buy Box win rate dashboard.

title: Seller success formula
supports: Fetched. Walmart internal study (November 2023 to November 2024): sellers meeting all five Seller Performance Standards averaged 40% more views, 40% more orders, 30% higher GMV and 10% higher customer rating than those who did not.

title: Commissie (commission)
supports: Fetched (Dutch). Listing is free; commission is a fixed amount per item plus a percentage by item type; the percentage is charged on the sales price including VAT; example range for kitchen items 5% to 12.5% plus €0.05 to €0.95; worked example; temporary lower commission when the price is at or below a set price point.

title: General Product Safety Regulation
supports: Fetched (Dutch). New listings without manufacturer details not allowed online since 5 March 2026; EU responsible person required since 1 April 2026; existing listings without manufacturer details phased out; manufacturer name, address and electronic address and EU responsible person details required.

title: Verantwoordelijke marktdeelnemers (DSA)
supports: Fetched (Dutch). Sellers record their EU responsible economic operators and link them to products, per item, in bulk by Excel with EAN codes, or through the Retailer API.

title: Servicenormen (service norms)
supports: Fetched (Dutch). Nine service norms (on-time items, cancellations, track and trace, returns, customer questions, phone availability, rating, response time, NPS after contact) affect sales and the buy box; thresholds are in the seller account, not on the page.

title: Partnership models
supports: Fetched. Wholesale, Partner Program (partner sets its own prices and keeps control of assortment and logistics) and Connected Retail (Zalando deducts commission; rate not published); Zalando invites brands and does not accept direct applications; 25 markets.

title: Informing Businesses about the INFORM Consumers Act
supports: Fetched. In effect 27 June 2023; high-volume seller test (200 or more sales and $5,000 or more in any 12 months of the past 24); information marketplaces collect and verify within 10 days; annual certification; disclosure for $20,000 or more; suspension after notice; civil penalty $53,088 per violation for marketplaces (January 2025 figure).

title: What third-party sellers need to know about the INFORM Consumers Act
supports: Fetched. Seller view: bank account, tax ID and contact details to provide; respond to certification requests within 10 days; home-based sellers may show only country and state with a contact method; marketplaces must suspend sales after notice if information is not provided.

title: The DSA's impact on digital platforms
supports: Fetched (last update 6 November 2026). Marketplaces must have sellers give verified identity information before they sell, so buyers can identify who is responsible; when an illegal product is sold, marketplaces notify buyers, identify the seller and offer redress.

title: Digital Services Act: questions and answers
supports: Fetched. The DSA covers online marketplaces; all regulated services had to comply by 17 February 2024; small and micro enterprises are exempt from some rules.

title: DAC7
supports: Fetched. Directive (EU) 2021/514 in force 1 January 2023; platforms report seller identity and the consideration paid to each seller, including for sales of goods; first exchange at the end of February 2024.

title: Check if you need to register as a digital platform operator
supports: Fetched (last updated 21 July 2026). UK platforms collect, check and report seller details to HMRC; sellers of goods are not reported if they receive €2,000 (about £1,700) or less for fewer than 30 sales in a year.

title: Understanding your Form 1099-K
supports: Fetched (last reviewed or updated 28 October 2026). Payment apps and online marketplaces report payments for goods or services that total over $20,000 in more than 200 transactions.

title: One Stop Shop
publisher: European Commission (VAT One Stop Shop portal)
supports: Fetched. OSS from 1 July 2021; EUR 10,000 threshold for intra-EU distance sales by a supplier in one Member State; Union, non-Union and Import schemes; marketplaces (electronic interfaces) are deemed suppliers for imports in consignments up to EUR 150 and for intra-EU supplies by sellers established outside the EU.

title: Consumer Reviews and Testimonials Rule: Questions and Answers
supports: Fetched. Rule in effect 21 October 2024; bans fake reviews, incentives conditioned on a particular sentiment, review suppression by threats or intimidation, and undisclosed insider reviews; general requests to all buyers are allowed.

title: Open letter to online retailers: including mandatory delivery fees in the total price
supports: Fetched (2 November 2026). Applies to marketplace operators as well as shops; where traders have their own delivery charges, the delivery price should be in the total price of each product; the total must appear at every stage.

title: Pricing (Uber Eats for merchants, US)
supports: Fetched (page undated). Lite 20%, Plus 25% and Premium 30% marketplace fees; pickup fee 7%, or 10% without validated in-store pricing; self-delivery fee 15%; some cities have lower Lite rates.

title: Guarantees and returns (right of withdrawal)
supports: Fetched (last checked 28/04/2026). 14-day right to cancel online purchases from a trader; purchases from private individuals, including some on marketplaces, are not covered.
